title: How to Go Viral on Instagram (6s reel)
notes: Reviewer-gated pipeline; defects caught & fixed: VO pace/trailing-silence, headline overflow, low audio gain (+7dB), glow sawtooth. A/V synced to VO pauses.

**Text-only evaluation — video not viewed** (no tools permitted), so post_production, visuals, voiceover_quality, and qa_at_each_step are scored 0.0 as *unverifiable*, not as observed failures. Treat combined_score 2.2/7.0 as a floor, not a verdict; re-run with video access.

**Accuracy 0.85:** Overfit-to-fixed-eval-set → holdout split is correct; "locked pile leaks when you tune to please it" is a valid test-set-contamination caveat. Minor: 20 examples is thin to split; unstated.

**Objectives 0.5:** learning_outcomes list was empty, so coverage cannot be assessed against stated LOs. Script does teach WHAT/WHY/HOW of holdout sets coherently.

**Storytelling 0.85:** Single invented protagonist (Ali, per house rule), one concrete scenario (grading assistant) carried start→finish, friction→fix→failure mode→payoff arc, leads with the tension. Docked for no explicit hook framing and a compressed payoff.

**Accuracy 0.85** — overfitting-to-a-fixed-eval-set is correctly explained; train/test split and test-set leakage caveat are sound. Slight simplification: "learned those twenty answers" is loose phrasing for tuning-to-the-set, and only 20 examples is thin, but nothing false.

**Objectives 0.7** — no learning_outcomes supplied, so coverage cannot be assessed against stated LOs; scored neutrally. Topic ("when a good eval score lies") is fully delivered: symptom, cause, fix, failure mode.

**Storytelling 0.9** — one invented protagonist (Ali) followed in depth on one concrete task; friction→fix→structure→failure mode→payoff all present, WHY and HOW both explained. Docked slightly: opens with setup rather than leading with the answer.

**Post-production 0.95 / QA 0.95** — all 8 mechanical checks pass (1920x1080, h264/yuv420p, 30fps, AAC, clips==beats 12, audio integrity, duration 79.6s ≈ VO 74.6s + bumpers, bumpers present).

**Visuals 0.75** — cannot verify safe zone, font sizes, or diagram legibility from this evidence; beat/mode mix (5 scene, 4 info, 3 ali) is well varied and each sentence has its own visual. Scored conservatively for lack of frame-level evidence.

**Voiceover 0.85** — audio-integrity check confirms all 12 beats have real, sane-length VO with sane totals; clarity, pacing, and pronunciation not directly verifiable.

Status: PASS (5.95 ≥ 4.9 threshold; ≥5.5 = publish immediately). No failing factors (<0.6). Low-scoring (<0.8): objectives_coverage 0.7, visuals 0.75 — both evidence-limited, not observed defects.

**Accuracy 0.9** — overfitting-to-a-fixed-eval-set and the train/holdout split are correctly explained; the holdout-leaks caveat is right. No stats to verify; 'twenty examples' is illustrative.

**Objectives 0.8** — no learning outcomes supplied, so scored against the stated topic ('when a good eval score lies'), which is fully taught: symptom, cause, fix, failure mode. Slightly under 0.9 because 'how to split' is asserted, not shown.

**Storytelling 0.9** — single invented protagonist (Ali) followed in depth through one grading-assistant scenario; friction→fix→structure→failure mode→payoff all present; leads with the concrete anomaly. WHY (wrong grades reach a real teacher) and HOW (tune on one pile, measure on the locked one) both explicit. Not 1.0: hook is gentle rather than answer-first.

**Post-production 0.95** and **QA 0.95** — all mechanical checks pass (1920x1080, h264/yuv420p, 30fps, AAC, clips==beats 12, audio integrity, sane duration, bumpers present).

**Voiceover 0.85** — audio integrity confirms all 12 beats have real, sane-length VO and duration matches (74.6s VO ≈ 12 beats); delivery clarity/pacing cannot be heard, so held just below the mechanical tier.

**Visuals 0.7** — cannot be assessed: only mode labels and generic descriptions ('illustrated scene', 'infographic: gauge') are available. No frames, safe-zone, typography, or color data. Scored neutrally per instructions, not as a defect.

Status: PASS (6.05 ≥ 4.9 threshold; ≥5.5 = publish immediately). Failing factors: 0. Below-0.8 factors: visuals (0.7, unassessable). Remediation not required.

**Strong.** Single invented protagonist (Ali) followed in depth through ONE scenario: friction (90 min) → fix (11s) → failure (raw print, period 2) → structure (write 3 things machine can't know, then edit) → second failure mode (drops editing when tired) → payoff. WHAT/WHY/HOW all present; lands the task-vs-job distinction concretely.

**Accuracy 0.85** — claims are narrative, not statistical; "eleven seconds" and "the eleven" are plausible but unverifiable, and "the eleven" is introduced without antecedent (beat 16).

**Objectives 0.7** — `learning_outcomes` is empty, so coverage cannot be measured against stated LOs; scored neutrally. The implicit outcome is taught well.

**Visuals 0.8 / VO 0.85** — cannot view the file; scored from mechanical checks (1920x1080, yuv420p, 30fps, AAC, 20 clips == 20 beats, all beats have real audio, 136.8s ≈ 131.9s VO + bumpers) plus sensible mode variety (12 scene / 4 info / 4 ali). Safe zone, typography, and delivery not directly verifiable.

**Post-production 0.95 / QA 0.95** — every mechanical check passed, including audio integrity, duration sanity, and brand bumpers.

**Accuracy:** Claims are conceptually sound — inter-rater agreement as the real test of a rubric, observability, and criterion overlap double-penalising a single flaw. Numbers are internally consistent (3.4 vs 2.1 → 19/20). Minor: the four checks are never enumerated in the VO, so beat 10 leans on unseen on-screen text.

**Objectives:** The single LO (rewrite a vague standard as observable, independently-checkable criteria) is taught end-to-end: friction (two graders disagree) → fix (four observable checks) → structure → failure mode (11 blurry criteria) → payoff (hand it to anyone). Held just under 1.0 because the learner hears the criteria described but never hears them stated.

**Post-production / QA:** All mechanical checks pass — 1920x1080, h264/yuv420p, 30fps, AAC, 22 clips == 22 beats, audio integrity on every spoken beat, duration 157.8s ≈ 152.8s VO + bumpers, bumpers present. No evidence of any gate skipped.

**Visuals:** Cannot be assessed from this evidence — no frames, no safe-zone/typography/SVG measurements available. Scored near-neutral. Positive signal only: 8 varied info templates (gauge, twocard, checks, statement, fourparts, quote) and mode alternation across scene/ali/info, so composition is unlikely to be monotonous.

**Storytelling:** Strongest factor. ONE invented protagonist (Ali) on ONE concrete task (20 Urdu comprehension questions) carried all 22 beats; Sara is a foil, not a character switch. No domain-hopping. Mandatory QUESTION→REVEAL present (beat 12 question, beat 13 reveal with reasoning). Closing line lands the WHY.

**Voiceover:** Audio integrity confirmed mechanically and pacing is sane (152.8s / 22 beats ≈ 6.9s per sentence, deliberate not rushed). Delivery quality, pronunciation, and breathing pauses are not observable from text, so scored on the mechanical evidence alone rather than penalised.

(Notes exceed the 500-char guideline in order to document every sub-0.8 score with evidence, per the scoring rules.)

**Accuracy** 0.9 — no factual claims to verify; internal logic is sound (self-check critique is correct). The "real set would put about forty" mid-band figure is an unsourced heuristic, hence not 1.0.

**Objectives** 1.0 — the single LO is fully hit: reviewer shifts from producing to designing checks (beats 12–13), and beat 19 names the check that survives a confidently-wrong AI (independent colleague).

**Storytelling** 0.95 — one named invented protagonist (Ali), one concrete scenario, full friction→fix→structure→failure-mode→payoff arc, mandatory QUESTION→REVEAL at beats 17–18.

**Visuals** 0.8 — cannot be seen; scored from beat plan only (good info/scene/ali mix, 6 varied info templates, no text-heavy beats). Not verifiable from evidence.

**Post-production / VO / QA** — all mechanical checks pass: 1920x1080 h264 yuv420p, 30fps, AAC, 22 clips == 22 beats, all beats have real VO, duration 164.8s vs 159.8s VO plus bumpers. Audio loudness, sync tightness, and colour were not measurable here.
